name: Antimilitarism
summary: Antimilitarism opposes militarism: a society in which war or preparation for war dominates politics, and the political power of a large standing army. It is not pacifism: the defining sources accept citizen militias and some wars, and the socialist tradition (Liebknecht's Militarism and Anti-Militarism, the Second International's congress resolutions) ties militarism to capitalism and class rule.
scope: The reference definition (the Oxford Companion entry) and the socialist antimilitarism of the Second International as set out in Karl Liebknecht's 1907 Militarism and Anti-Militarism (congress resolutions 1868-1900, the German minimum programme). The American tradition against standing armies and Eisenhower's farewell warning are named by the Oxford Companion but state no further positions here. Excluded: absolute pacifism, and the platforms of peace organisations or the positions of states such as Japan (Article 9), which are coatracks.
